result.response:
I have resolved the issue by converting non-ASCII hostnames and domain names to punycode (IDNA) before constructing email headers.

### Root Cause
When system hostnames or domain names contain non-ASCII characters, generating the `Message-ID` header with non-ASCII domain characters caused header validation/encoding to fail with a `UnicodeEncodeError` when non-UTF-8 encodings (such as `iso-8859-1`) were used for email messages.

### Changes Made
1. [django/core/mail/utils.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-gakqaeii/django/core/mail/utils.py#L13-L18): In [`CachedDnsName.get_fqdn`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-gakqaeii/django/core/mail/utils.py#L14-L18), encode the output of `socket.getfqdn()` using `.encode('idna').decode('ascii')`.
2. [django/core/mail/message.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-gakqaeii/django/core/mail/message.py#L257-L261): Convert `DNS_NAME` to IDNA ASCII punycode when generating `Message-ID` in [`EmailMessage.message`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-gakqaeii/django/core/mail/message.py#L239-L265).
3. [tests/mail/tests.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-gakqaeii/tests/mail/tests.py#L405-L417): Added `test_unicode_dns` to verify that non-ASCII DNS names/hostnames are correctly encoded to punycode `xn--...` when creating email messages.
